
### distributing Bellman-Ford outline (1)  {.smaller}


* [on each node A run:]{.fragment fragment-index=1 .custom .myem-only}
* repeatedly:
* for each link <em>from A</em> (going to B, distance c) 

   * for each node X:
   * if $c + d(B, X) < d(A, X)$, <br>
   * then $d(A,X) \leftarrow c+d(B,X)$, $p(A,X) = B$
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* [on node A: track $d(A, X)$, $p(A, X)$]{.fragment fragment-index=2 .custom .myem-only}
* [node A needs to get $d(B, X)$ to run algorithm]{.fragment fragment-index=3 .custom .myem-only}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="The same graph (with A, B, C, D connected via weighte directed edges) as before, and an uninitialized table of distances and next hops for every ordered pair of nodes."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Each node A, B, C, D has its distances and next hops for each node (a row of the original Bellman-Ford table of routes)."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Node C sends an update to node D: 'I'm C, costs: C=0' (copying its distance vector)"}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="Node D uses this update to set its route to C to have cost 5 (0+the cost of its edge to C) and next hop of C."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="Node D sends an update to node B: 'I'm D, costs: D=0, C=5' (copying its distance vector)."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-6.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6 fig-alt="Node B uses the update from D to set routes: to C via D at cost 6 (5 +the cost of the B to D edge), to D via D at cost 1 (0+the cost of the B to D edge)."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-7.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=7 fig-alt="Node C also sends updates to nodes A and B: 'I'm C, costs: C=0'."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-8.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=8 fig-alt="As a result, A updates its route to C (cost 1=0+1 via C, 1 is the A to C edge cost), and B updates its route to C (cost 2=0+2 via C)."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-9.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=9 fig-alt="Node D sends another update to node C: 'I'm D, costs: D=0,C=infinity'. C's cost is passed as infinity despite D's route to C being cost 5 via C."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford.figure-10.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=10 fig-alt="As a result of D's update from C, C sets its cost to D to be 4=0+4 (link cost) via D."}

:::

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford2.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="The same graph (network with costs with A, B, C, D)."}

All the distane vectors are filled in completely, except D's distance vector has entries of 'infinity via nothing' for its route to A, B, and C."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford2.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Node C, with current distance vector: 1 via A to A, 2 via B to B, 0 vi C to C, 4 via D to D, sends an update to D: 'I'm C, costs: A=1, B=2, C=0, D=5.'"}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford2.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="As a result of C's update it fills in entries in its distance vector that were infinity: 6 via C to A, 7 via C to B, 5 via C to C. Each of these add 5 (the edge cost from D to C) to the distance vector sent by C."}

![](/routing-dv/texfig/distributing-bellman-ford2.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="Node B sends an update 'I'm B, costs: A=4,B=0,C=2,D=5' to D. D has a current distance vector: 6 via C to C, 7 via C to B, 5 via C to C, 0 via D to D. The link from D to B has a weight of 2."}
